headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/capability conflict: Superset can call APIs while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge list, so interaction risk is limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces, while superset only exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress. There is no documented shared channel or default ingestion path between them, so a prompt-injection bridge is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator copies list content from awesome-selfhosted into Superset prompts or dashboards, injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the list and Superset in separate workspaces.
Disable any automation that pastes repository text into prompts.
Review any custom connector that imports markdown into Superset.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The pair does not show shared data classes or a shared workspace, and awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable. Superset can call APIs and has allowlisted egress, so leakage would require an external bridge that feeds sensitive files into Superset; the profiles do not show that bridge, so the blast radius appears limited and indirect.
conditions: IF an operator places sensitive documents into a Superset-connected dataset or API payload, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not load sensitive files into Superset datasets.
Restrict API credentials to non-sensitive sources.
Audit outbound API destinations in Superset.
Separate any knowledge-list curation from analytics workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filters on imports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and requests no permissions, while superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted network egress. That means overlapping write conflict is not documented; any conflict would require an external orchestrator granting both write access to the same mutable resource, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF both agents are wired to the same mutable API or database through an external orchestrator, concurrent writes can conflict.
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents write access to the same resource.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
Add manual approval before any write action.
Check for duplicate automation against the same API.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a static knowledge list, not an action-taking agent, and superset is a data-engineering tool with API access. A cascading error would require an external workflow that treats the list as authoritative input for Superset actions; that pathway is not documented, so the risk is limited.
conditions: IF a workflow converts entries from awesome-selfhosted into Superset configuration or actions without review, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on imported entries.
Validate any imported metadata against source docs.
Keep generated actions read-only by default.
Log provenance for every imported item.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before API actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies are documented for either agent, and awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable repository list while superset is an open-source analytics tool. With no compliance-sensitive flow shown, a residency or certification mismatch is not evidenced.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through Superset or a hosted mirror of awesome-selfhosted, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of this pair until policies are defined.
Review hosting region and retention settings.
Record any compliance obligations in deployment notes.
